sources.entry: crterm - Beautifully opinionated terminal emulator, with advanced session navigation and GPU-accelerated retro presets.

summary.one_liner: crterm is a macOS terminal emulator with a vertical tab rail, command-history and session search, split panes, tear-off windows, and optional CRT-style looks.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a vertical sidebar of sessions showing live titles, previews, and bell attention badges. A ⌘K palette searches all sessions, and ⌘⇧K / ⌘⌥K search command history for the focused terminal or all terminals and recall a command to the prompt; shell integration is auto-injected for zsh. Sessions can be split right or down, and dragged out of the sidebar into their own windows and back. Links can be opened with ⌘-click or the context menu, and ⌥-click moves the cursor on the command line. The README also describes an Auto theme that follows macOS light/dark appearance, a CRT mode, a Degauss option, and rendering via Metal with CoreText, with a platform-independent emulation core that has its own parser, grid, and fuzzing harness.
use_cases: Searching past shell commands and re-running them
Managing many terminal sessions in tabs
Splitting one terminal window into multiple panes
Opening folders or scripts from Finder in a terminal
Using a retro CRT-styled terminal on macOS
how_to_run: Scripts/build.sh # Debug build; add `release` for Release
Scripts/test.sh # run the test suites CI runs
stack: Swift (implied by macOS app and Xcode-style build)
notable: Command history search across one or all terminals, with zsh shell integration auto-injected
Tear-off windows: drag a session out of the sidebar and back to recombine
Option-click to move the cursor on the command line or in full-screen editors
Scripts dropped on the Dock icon run in their own session that stays open with exit status
Metal GPU rendering driven directly by session updates, with a separate platform-independent emulation core
caveats: Requires macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later and Apple Silicon
Build-from-source setup details are in ARCHITECTURE.md and RELEASING.md, not in the README
